_about: What each check stands on, in the order it is looked for: the editor's documentation, public reports, a local test. A level left out is not claimed. Measured precision is in precision.json.

01-claude-md-case.documented_note: The memory page names CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md and says nothing about case (read 2026-10-08).
01-claude-md-case.reported_note: Users report the lowercase file is found on macOS and Windows (case-insensitive filesystems) and not on Linux.

tested.how: A codeword in claude.md, then in CLAUDE.md; a session asked for it without reading files.

01-claude-md-case.precision_note: 44 of 46 findings were instruction files that Linux does not load; 2 were a personal cheatsheet and user documentation. 44 public repositories, 2026-10-08, labelled by the assistant, not blind.

23-agent-tools.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (an Agent(...) list applies only to an agent run as the main thread)
23-agent-tools.documented_note: The alias Task -> Agent was documented on the sub-agents page and is no longer (read 2026-10-08).

tested.how: deny ["Task"], deny ["Agent"] and no rule, each in a fresh project; a session asked to spawn a subagent.
tested.result: Task and Agent rules both remove the Agent tool; without a rule the subagent runs.

43-mcp-credential-var.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (Credential variables that read as empty: five names, given as examples)
43-mcp-credential-var.documented_note: The page lists ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, HTTPS_PROXY and NPM_TOKEN after "such as"; the other eight names the check matches are measured, not documented.

tested.how: claude mcp list with a disposable CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, against a local HTTP server that logs the headers it receives; each name set and unset, with and without :-default.
tested.result: AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN arrive empty in every case; AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN and a name of the project's own expand, and :-DEF gives DEF.

42-permissions-rule.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (auto mode drops `Agent` allow rules); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (the Manual-mode table does not list the Agent tool among those that ask; Agent(<name>) rules are described for deny, parameter rules for deny and ask)
42-permissions-rule.documented_note: Scope of this entry: the NOTICE on a whole-tool Agent allow rule ("Agent", "Agent(*)"). The other 42-permissions-rule findings cite the permissions page directly. Read 2026-10-09. Also the `$HOME` advice: the permissions page names `//`, `~/`, `/` and relative paths, and no variable.

tested.how: claude -p with --setting-sources "" (no permission rule at all), in default and in dontAsk mode, asked to delegate to a sub-agent; then the same with --disallowedTools "Agent(general-purpose)".
tested.result: Without any rule the Agent tool was called, the sub-agent started and answered, permission_denials empty, in both modes. With the deny rule the call was refused: "Agent type 'general-purpose' has been denied by permission rule".

tested_home_variable.how: claude -p --model claude-haiku-5-5 --setting-sources project --settings <file>, HOME set to a temporary folder holding probe/secret.txt (also the working directory), asked to Read that file; three settings files: no rule, deny Read($HOME/probe/secret.txt), deny Read(~/probe/secret.txt). One run each.
tested_home_variable.result: No rule: the content was returned. Deny Read($HOME/...): the content was returned, permission_denials empty. Deny Read(~/...): refused, "File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings."
